headline: Oil and gold keep climbing while PSX hunts for a floor after three straight down days.
summary: Global markets paused Friday - Wall Street dipped while oil and gold both climbed, showing the Middle East risk premium is alive, not fading. PSX has closed lower three sessions straight, though Friday's late reading clawed back into the green (not yet a confirmed close). SBP is holding its rate at 11.5% with reserves inching up to $17.08bn, and a new plan to settle part of the gas circular debt is feeding extra dividends to OGDC and PPL. The desk's lean: stay selective, favour energy names riding oil and the debt settlement, and stay wary of power and refining names still absorbing cost pressure.

sectors.name: E&P (Oil & Gas Exploration)
sectors.why: Brent sits at a fresh $94.4 and a new Rs540bn extra-dividend plan tied to the gas circular-debt settlement flows straight to OGDC and PPL, which were among the only names giving the index buying support this week.

sectors.name: Commercial Banks
sectors.why: The held 11.5% policy rate and rising T-bill cutoffs (up to 11.99% on 12-month paper) support carry income on bank balance sheets, but UBL, HBL and Bank AL Habib were themselves among the heaviest index drags this week, so the desk isn't chasing the sector broadly.

sectors.name: Power / IPPs
sectors.why: Hub Power was one of the week's heaviest single-stock drags, and total energy-sector circular debt still sits near Rs5.29tn even after the partial gas settlement.

sectors.name: Refineries
sectors.why: Refiners just absorbed a government-directed 8.2% cut to diesel prices, a near-term margin squeeze for ATRL, NRL, PRL and Cnergyico.

watchlist.angle: The desk's 'volume leads price' pattern (obv_divergence_up) is triggering on BML right now - a high-confidence signal that has won 97% of the time over 89 past trades on BML's own history, still profitable out-of-sample. Fundamentals screen attractive: a cheap P/E of 6.52 against a strong 32% net margin (though it pays no dividend, so the case rests entirely on the price working).
watchlist.risk: Macro's own sector read flags broad banks to avoid beyond the carry angle this week - UBL, HBL and BAFL were the index's heaviest drags in this same stretch, so a single stock's chart trigger is fighting a sector headwind.

watchlist.angle: A 52-week-high breakout is triggering on ATRL (medium confidence, 57% win rate over 30 past trades, still profitable out-of-sample), and ATRL was named as a green mover in Friday's midday session. Results are due 2026-08-25 (four sessions out, estimate unconfirmed). Fundamentals are mixed - cheap on P/E (5.17) but thin on margin (7.4%) with a negligible 0.48% dividend.
watchlist.risk: Macro's sector tilt explicitly flags refineries to avoid right now - ATRL just absorbed the government-directed diesel price cut, a direct hit to refining margins that could outweigh the technical breakout.

watchlist.angle: Results are due today (2026-08-21, estimate unconfirmed), and ENGROH was one of two names given a full same-day Desk Room bull/bear debate (139 claims resolved, no flip either way). It was also one of the few names providing buying support in Thursday's close. Fundamentals rate attractive - a cheap trailing P/E of 5.16 and a healthy 10.2% net margin.
watchlist.risk: ENGROH's forward P/E (7.34) is actually higher than its trailing P/E (5.16) - the market is already pricing in slower forward earnings, which cuts against the 'cheap' read, and there's no dividend to cushion a miss.

watchlist.angle: HUBC was the other name given a full same-day Desk Room debate session, with results due 2026-08-28. Fundamentals rate attractive - a strong 64.8% net margin and a dividend (7.04% yield) covered by a modest 43% payout ratio.
watchlist.risk: Macro's sector tilt explicitly flags power/IPP names to avoid - HUBC was named as one of the heaviest index drags this week, and sector-wide circular debt (~Rs5.29tn) remains a live overhang despite the partial gas settlement.

watchlist.angle: MARI sits inside macro's own 'favoured' E&P tilt - elevated Brent plus the new gas-settlement dividend plan - and carries a confirmed, primary-source dividend event: Rs18.7/share (2.8% yield) with book closure 2026-09-22 and buy-by 2026-09-19, per dps.psx.com.pk. It was also named as a green mover in Friday's session.
watchlist.risk: Fundamentals rate only mixed - a P/E of 9.37 isn't especially cheap, and the 51.69% payout ratio leaves less room than some peers if oil reverses.

catalysts.event: MSCI Frontier Market Small Cap reconstitution effective date (AIRLINK added, Biafo Industries removed)
Confirmed book closure, Rs18.7/share dividend (2.8% yield), buy-by 2026-09-19

risks: The desk's geo-risk gauge still reads 57/100 'moderate' - not 'low' - with Brent at $94.4 and gold's safe-haven bid still building; a further Strait of Hormuz escalation would hit the rupee and import costs before it helps any single stock.

PSX has closed lower three sessions running (-1.41%, -0.62%, -0.14%), and Friday's later, greener reading (+0.33% as of a 4:50pm checkpoint) is not yet a confirmed official close - a real reversal isn't proven yet.

Energy-sector circular debt actually widened to roughly Rs5.29tn in FY26 despite the new Rs1.49tn gas settlement - the power/IPP overhang dragging on HUBC and peers has been only partly addressed, not resolved.
